note: The Studio's landing page (Zach's N-3, 2026-10-17): golden examples, the inputs drawn for the user, markers first. Each item is a design file beside this one; the Studio opens a copy (GET /api/gallery, POST /api/gallery/open). `look` is the card's 'what to look at'; `actions` are its buttons: 3d (the 3D view), sheet (Export > Sticker sheet...), send (Export > Send to PrusaSlicer...), ids (Renumber all). `lint` (2026-10-17): the error-level messages an example shows on purpose (the page lint's red row; it still builds); absent = 0.

groups.title: Markers by hand
groups.line: Type first, then the inner numbers; the outer size follows.

items.name: basics_single
items.title: A single marker
items.line: Single, Marker size typed: the tile and the trimmed plate follow.
items.look: Typed: Single, DICT_4X4_50, Marker size 30 mm. The 0.6 mm printer's cells are whole 0.68 mm lines, so it builds 28.56 mm (the Size row says so). The outer size is derived: one module of white each side makes a 38.1 mm tile, and Trim excess cuts the 50 mm plate down to it. Type another Marker size in the inspector.

items.name: basics_grid
items.title: A grid board
items.line: Grid, 3 × 2 at 12.24 mm: the board is 46.2 × 31.3 mm.
items.look: Typed: Grid, Marker size 12.24 mm, 3 × 2. On a sketch profile the typed count is kept; the board with its white border, 46.2 × 31.3 mm, is the outer size and the plate is trimmed to it. Change Columns × rows or the Marker size.

items.name: basics_charuco
items.title: A ChArUco board
items.line: ChArUco, checker 16.32, marker 12.24, 4 × 3.
items.look: Typed: ChArUco, Checker 16.32 mm, Marker 12.24 mm, 4 × 3. The board is 65.3 × 49.0 mm with no outer border: its six inner corners are the checker's. The plate is trimmed to the board.

groups.title: Inkjet stickers (2D)
groups.line: Vinyl sticker paper: the black printed into it, the page it prints on, moved by hand.

items.name: inkjet_paper
items.title: The paper and the black inside it
items.line: One paper body t thick; the black t/2 into it, flush with the top.
items.look: Make rule 2, what every new inkjet sticker gets: the sticker is ONE paper body as thick as the paper (t), the whole cut outline; the black is printed t/2 into its top, flush, no film on it; the tag frame (OpenCV's) sits on the paper's top, t over the face. Left, real vinyl: 0.10 mm (the default; measure yours, liner off). Middle and right: the same on 2 mm 'paper', exaggerated so the 3D view shows the black sunk into the white. Select one: the Inkjet tab's grey line under Paper thickness gives the depths.

items.name: inkjet_presets
items.title: Letter and A4 vinyl
items.line: The two inkjet presets, and a tag's own paper thickness.
items.look: The preset is the machine: 'Inkjet · Letter vinyl' and 'Inkjet · A4 vinyl' (600 dpi, whole dots, 0.10 mm vinyl, 10 mm page margins). Select a tag: Made by reads Inkjet printer, and the Inkjet tab has Paper thickness (with its stock suggestions), Paper size and Page margins. Right: this tag's own 0.18 mm (vinyl + laminate), an override on the tag only: its Preset row reads This tag (modified).

items.name: page_lint
items.title: Too big for the page
items.line: A typed size over the page is flagged red and still built; Auto stops at the page.
items.look: Left: a typed 200 mm marker makes a 266.5 mm sticker, over what Letter prints (195.9 × 233.4 mm inside 10 mm margins, the footer and the scale bars) whichever way round: the Marker size row is red like a linter, the cut line red, and the tag is still built (the sheet will not place it). Right: Auto size on a 300 mm face stops at the page, a 195.7 mm sticker, and the Size row says it was capped.

items.name: shift
items.title: Shift by hand
items.line: Shift X / Y move a sticker off where the fit puts it.
items.look: Left, where the fit puts it: centred. Middle, Shift 20, 8 mm along the face's own x and y. Right, on a disc (Perimeter = Profile), shifted 12 mm down. Select a sticker and drag its crosshair (0.5 mm steps, Alt for free), or type Shift X / Y on the Marker tab; a sticker shifted off its face is warned.

items.name: two_ways
items.title: 3D printed and inkjet
items.line: The same 30 mm marker, made by two presets.
items.look: Both tags ask for a 30 mm single. Left, the 0.6 mm 3D printer: whole 0.68 mm lines give 28.56 mm, the black printed on the plate (3D badge). Right, the Letter vinyl inkjet preset: whole 600 dpi dots give 29.97 mm on 0.10 mm vinyl, the black printed 0.05 mm into it, cut along the marker (2D badge). Select one: Made by under the Preset says how it is made.

items.name: ids
items.title: Unique across 2D and 3D
items.line: Seven tags made without ids, all #0: Renumber all makes them unique.
items.look: Every tag here was made without an id, so each starts at #0: the IDs table on the left marks the duplicates. Press Renumber all: the 3D tags and the stickers get one numbering per dictionary family (a sticker #3 and a printed #3 would be one duplicate). 'other' is DICT_6X6, a family of its own, so it keeps #0.

groups.title: Auto-placement on profiles
groups.line: The largest clear rectangle, holes avoided or ignored, 0° or 90°.

items.name: faces
items.title: The largest clear rectangle
items.line: Zach's disc, a D-shape, an L and a plate with a hole.
items.look: Nothing is typed: each Auto size fills its face's largest clear square, holes and notches avoided. Zach's Ø53 disc with four holes: a 37.4 mm square, a 24.48 mm marker. The D-shape 30.7 mm, the plate beside its hole 31.0 mm, the L in one leg. Drag a shape's handle (select the shape, not the tag) and the marker re-places live.

items.name: faces_boards
items.title: Boards on odd faces
items.line: A ring, a hexagon, a slot, a notch, a strip and a triangle.
items.look: A board on Auto takes as many markers as fit in the face's largest clear rectangle: the strip gets a long row, the notched plate a board beside the notch. Where Auto's cells come out under the preset's 2.0 mm minimum, the Size row warns and names a checker size that passes.

items.name: holes
items.title: Holes: avoid or ignore
items.line: The same faces with Holes on Avoid (left) and Ignore (right).
items.look: Avoid keeps the tile clear of every hole; Ignore lets the tile cover them and says so (the covered hole is dashed). The plate's offset hole: 24.48 mm becomes 32.64 mm; the disc's centre hole: 12.24 mm becomes 24.48 mm; the ChArUco: 2 × 4 becomes 4 × 3. Switch Holes in the inspector to watch it re-place.

items.name: angles
items.title: 0° or 90°
items.line: The fit turns the board with the face; the Origin turns the marker.
items.look: The fit tries the tile at 0° and at 90° and keeps the one with more markers: the same Auto grid is 4 × 1 on the wide plate and 1 × 4 on the tall one. On the right, Origin 0 and 90: the marker and its OpenCV frame (x red, y green) a quarter turn apart on the face; the corner triangle shows which way.

groups.title: Labels
groups.line: On the black or the white, auto or by hand; a ChArUco label in a black square.

items.name: labels_where
items.title: On the black, on the white
items.line: 3D tags and stickers, each label where it prints.
items.look: A 3D label cut out of the black strokes at least 1.1 cell lines (rule 5): 3.74 mm letters at 0.68 mm lines, so the black row must be a 7.48 mm module (the 44.88 mm marker). On the white: below and to the right. Stickers print much smaller letters: '#3' on the black of a 22 mm sticker; on the white when Perimeter = Profile leaves white for it.

items.name: labels_place
items.title: Auto, or placed by hand
items.line: Auto picks the black or the white; Above; X / Y by hand.
items.look: Left, Auto: the black row is too small for the letters, so the label goes on the white and the Label row says why. Middle, Above with '#id + name'. Right, Placed by hand (X 12, Y -22 mm). Select a tag and drag its label on the canvas (0.25 mm steps).

items.name: labels_charuco
items.title: A ChArUco label
items.line: In a black square only: Auto, and dragged to another square.
items.look: A ChArUco label goes in a black square, never on the white. Left, Auto: the first black square that holds '#0-3'. Right, placed by hand (Placed: manual, X 24.48, Y -24.48 mm) in the bottom-right black square. Select it and drag the label into any other black square; a square too small refuses it with the reason.

items.name: marks
items.title: None, cut corner, triangle
items.line: The three marks on singles, a grid and a ChArUco.
items.look: Top: None, Cut white corner, Black triangle. Bottom: a grid and a ChArUco with the triangle. On a single or a grid the mark sits in the quiet zone's corner, so the marker's own squares are never cut. A ChArUco board has no white corner: its top-left black checker square loses its outer corner instead (the Corner mark row says so).

items.name: trim
items.title: Marker or Profile
items.line: A 3D plate trimmed or not; stickers cut as a rectangle or as the disc.
items.look: Top, 3D: Trim excess off keeps the 50 mm plate (Profile); on, the plate is cut to the 38.1 mm tile (Marker). Bottom, stickers on Zach's disc: Perimeter = Profile cuts along the disc and its four holes; Perimeter = Marker cuts the marker's rectangle. The cut lines are dashed grey.

items.name: forearm
items.title: The forearm box
items.line: Four ChArUco boards on the four sides of a 120 × 40 × 40 box.
items.look: One feature, four faces: each side gets its own board and its own ids (0, 6, 10, 16). In 2D the box is drawn as its net, each side hinged at a dashed line; in 3D the boards stand on their faces. Change one face's settings and the list splits into one feature per face.

groups.title: The sticker sheet
groups.line: Tight or spaced; a white margin round each sticker; cut lines on or off.

items.name: sheet_tight
items.title: Tight
items.line: Five stickers in shelves that share their cut lines.
items.look: Open the sheet: Tight packs the stickers in shelves where neighbours share a cut line (fewer cuts); the disc keeps its outline and hole as cut lines. The page carries the 100 mm bar to check the print scale.

items.name: sheet_spaced
items.title: Spaced
items.line: The same stickers with gaps, captions and crop marks.
items.look: Open the sheet: Spaced leaves gaps, puts the id and name under each sticker and crop marks at its corners. Switch Tight / Spaced, the page or the margin in the dialog.

items.name: sheet_options
items.title: Sticker margin and cut lines
items.line: The sheet's own options, not the tag's: 3 mm of white round each sticker.
items.look: Open the sheet: Sticker margin 3 mm puts white paper round each sticker, so its cut line moves 3 mm out (the disc's hole stays where it is); Cut lines off prints the stickers alone. Both moved from the tag to the sheet (Zach's Q7: "Only in export sheet"); a tag made before keeps its own margin.

items.name: send
items.title: Beds and Send
items.line: Four 3D tags for one bed.
items.look: Export › Send to PrusaSlicer… picks the physical printer (PrusaSlicer's current one first), a print preset that fits it and the white and black extruders, then writes a 3MF project with the colours set. Open PrusaSlicer is a tick in the dialog.
